violations.detail: crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs adds an email address outside the allow-list

producer_report.summary: The checks stage now uses the repository's CI result for the candidate. `Athena::with_ci_source` (run/mod.rs) picks the source and the wait together. With an https github.com origin it reads the push run on `athena/ci/<job id>` through `gh` and waits up to the new `[budget] ci_wait_s` (default 1500, set in athena.toml). The wait is one read every 20 seconds, 76 reads in all. With no GitHub origin, or in a nested run, it uses `NoCi` and one read with no pause. `check_and_verify` passes the candidate SHA to the new `routing::run_routed_recorded`, which returns the CI record when a green run was used. A green run skips the local checks, and the check notes name the CI run. The verifier gets `verify::reuse_statement` as one extra non-check entry, `ci-reuse`, in its check list. A red run comes back as failed check records, so the job is rejected with `check clippy failed` and no local run. A missing, cancelled, timed-out or other-SHA run falls back to the local checks. Tests drive `Athena::go` with a fake `gh::Runner` (`test_support::CiRunner`) read through a thread-local seam, with `early_seam` fakes installed first. Each test sets the wait pause to zero, so none sleeps, and with no runner installed the stand-in `NoGh` refuses every call. CHANGELOG has an entry that says a resumed job carries no reuse statement. All of cargo fmt, clippy and the policy scan pass, and `cargo test -p athena-core -p athena-data` passes (768 passed, 1 ignored in athena-core; 139 passed in athena-data). I also ran the full `cargo test --locked` once. It finished without a failure message, but the output was too large and unreadable under the file-access policy, so I did not see its per-crate summary.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new test through Athena::go with an https github.com origin, a fake gh::Runner replying a green push run for the candidate SHA (with a failed history job next to a successful 'fmt, clippy, tests' job), and early_seam recording fakes shows the recording local check executor is never called, and the recorded CheckRuns' notes name CI as their source.
criteria_check.evidence: run::tests::...::ci_green_run_is_reused_and_no_local_check_runs passes. It uses origin https://github.com/owner/repo and installs `early_seam::install` and `ci_runner_seam::install(CiRunner)` before `go`. The fake's jobs reply has 'the full history' failed beside 'fmt, clippy, tests' successful. The test asserts the local executor's call list is empty, state is Landed, three checks fmt/clippy/test passed, and each note contains 'CI run https://example.test/ci/10' and the pushed SHA. It also asserts the runs query carried `head_sha=<pushed SHA>` and `branch=athena/ci/<job id>`. Ran with `cargo test -p athena-core ci_`.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test with a red push run for the candidate SHA shows the job fails, the failure names the failing check, and no local check ran.
criteria_check.evidence: ci_red_run_fails_the_job_naming_the_check passes. State is Rejected (a local failure also ends Rejected), the local executor's call list is empty, `verification.reasons` contains 'check clippy failed', checks are fmt true, clippy false, test true, and the verifier brief has no reuse statement.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: tests with no run, a cancelled run, and a timed-out run for the SHA each show the local checks run as before and the job proceeds.
criteria_check.evidence: ci_without_a_usable_run_falls_back_to_local_checks loops over NoRun, Cancelled, TimedOut and OtherSha (a run for another SHA). Each case asserts the state is Landed, the local executor ran fmt, clippy, test, the notes carry no 'CI run', the fake gh was asked, and there is no reuse statement. The NoRun case also asserts the read count equals `ci_wait(1500).polls` (76).

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test with no GitHub origin (none or a local path) shows NoCi is used, the fake runner receives no call, and the wait is not applied (no sleeping, one read).
criteria_check.evidence: ci_no_github_origin_does_not_wait covers five origins (none, a local path, a lookalike local path, a gitlab URL, an example.com/github.com/... URL). The fake is set to answer green, yet its path log is empty, the local checks run, and the job lands. with_ci_source_pairs_the_source_with_its_wait calls `with_ci_source` directly: with no origin and with a non-GitHub path, the closure sees `Wait{polls:1,pause:ZERO}` and `fetch` returns None. With the GitHub origin, polls equals `ci_wait(1500).polls` (76) with a zero test pause, and a bound of 0 gives one read.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test shows that when CI is green the verifier's input contains the text from verify::reuse_statement for the candidate SHA.
criteria_check.evidence: ci_green_run_gives_the_verifier_the_reuse_statement builds the expected CiRecord (CI source, pushed SHA, run address, three success steps, 150 s), computes `verify::reuse_statement`, and asserts the captured verifier user_prompt contains that exact text. The local-fallback run's brief has no 'ci-reuse' entry.

criteria_check.criterion: run/mod.rs no longer passes routing::NoCi unconditionally at the run_routed call; a function with_ci_source picks the source and wait together (Grep `with_ci_source`), and the candidate SHA is what is passed to resolution.
criteria_check.evidence: Grep for `with_ci_source` in run/mod.rs finds the definition and the single call in `check_and_verify`. `routing::NoCi` appears in run/mod.rs only inside `with_ci_source`. The call passes `&c` (the candidate commit) to `run_routed_recorded`, which hands it to `resolve`. The green test shows the fake answers only for the pushed SHA, so the SHA is what was passed.

criteria_check.criterion: athena.toml (listed deliverable) sets the CI wait bound to 1500 seconds, and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (listed deliverable) has the matching schema field; the config round-trip/load tests still pass.
criteria_check.evidence: athena.toml [budget] has `ci_wait_s = 1500`. `Budget.ci_wait_s` in config.rs has a serde default of `DEFAULT_CI_WAIT_S` (1500). The new test `the_ci_wait_bound_is_in_athena_toml_and_defaults_when_missing` passes, and the full athena-data suite passed (139 tests).

criteria_check.criterion: Every new test with an https github.com origin installs both the gh::Runner fake and early_seam recording fakes (Grep `early_seam::install` in the new tests); no test reaches the network.
criteria_check.evidence: Every new test with a GitHub origin goes through the `ci_go` helper, which calls `early_seam::install` and `ci_runner_seam::install` before `go`. The with_ci_source test installs the runner seam and builds Athena without calling `go`, so it needs no early_seam. With no runner installed, with_ci_source uses `NoGh`, which refuses every call, so existing tests with a github.com origin cannot reach gh either. The existing origin tests still pass.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change that also states a resumed job carries no reuse statement.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Changed' has the new first entry. It describes the CI result use, `ci_wait_s`, the red and fallback rules, and says 'a resumed job whose recorded checks came from CI carries no reuse statement'.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`; all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. For my own part: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` passed. `cargo test --locked --quiet -p athena-core -p athena-data` passed. The full `cargo test --locked` ran once and showed no failure, but I could not read its saved output.

open_issues: I did not read the full `cargo test --locked` output (too large; the saved copy was outside the allowed directory). Athena's own run is the confirmation for the cli and cap crates.
Departure from the plan: crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs is unchanged. It needed no doc change, and `reuse_statement` is used as is.

Departure from the plan: crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs gets the new `GhClient::https_repository` and a small test module (`origin_tests`). The https-origin rule is copied from the private `early.rs::https_github_repository`, because early.rs and gh/mod.rs are out of scope. Both rules are pinned by tests over the same origin forms, but they could still drift apart.

Carried over from the plan: if the CI branch push fails (one warning line), the read finds no run and waits up to `ci_wait_s` (25 minutes by default) before falling back to the local checks. `push_ci_branch` returns nothing and early.rs is out of scope, so the checks stage cannot tell.

A resumed job takes its recorded checks and never reads CI, so a resumed job whose checks came from CI carries no reuse statement. This is stated in the CHANGELOG and matches the brief's out-of-scope list.
mistakes: I first ran the full `cargo test --locked` without `--quiet`, which made the output unreadable, so I had to rerun the core and data crates quietly.
learnings: `Docs` in run/tests.rs had a single check named `probe`, so `route.reuse` was false and CI was never consulted in any existing test. The new tests need the three-check variant (`routed: true`).
Finished.verification.reasons carries 'check <name> failed'. A red CI run ends Rejected, the same as a failing local check.
GhClient::api retries only a GhFailure with a transient status or text. A plain error from a fake runner is not retried, so a failing fake gives Missing at once.
The bash and file-access policy blocks reading saved tool output outside the working directory, so large test output cannot be re-read. Use `--quiet` for big runs.

Budget has deny_unknown_fields, and the real athena.toml is included by tests (REPO_CONFIG). A new field therefore needs a serde default and the matching athena.toml line. Keep a comment line from repeating the key name, because the new config test filters lines by prefix and asserts the name is gone.
desires: A way to read saved large tool output, or a default `--quiet` for long test runs.
